elements.element: Customer owns all deliverables created for it.
elements.evidence: Section 5.5 states that the Company owns “the Site” and “all other deliverables ... created by HDI for the Company under this Agreement.”

elements.element: Customer owns all work product created for it.
elements.evidence: Section 5.5 expressly gives the Company ownership of “all ... work product created by HDI for the Company under this Agreement.”

elements.element: Vendor assigns its ownership rights in the deliverables and work product to Customer.
elements.evidence: HDI “hereby assigns all such right, title and interest to the Company,” covering the previously identified Site, deliverables and work product.

elements.element: Vendor retains ownership of its pre-existing IP.
elements.evidence: Section 5.5 states that HDI retains ownership of its “pre-existing software, systems, tools and know-how.”

elements.element: Vendor grants Customer a licence to Vendor IP embedded in the deliverables.
elements.evidence: HDI grants the Company a licence to “any such HDI materials to the extent incorporated in the Site or in any deliverable.”

elements.element: The licence to embedded Vendor IP is perpetual.
elements.evidence: The embedded-materials licence is expressly “perpetual.”

elements.element: The licence to embedded Vendor IP is irrevocable.
elements.evidence: The embedded-materials licence is expressly “irrevocable.”

elements.element: The licence to embedded Vendor IP is royalty-free.
elements.evidence: The embedded-materials licence is expressly “royalty-free.”

elements.element: Customer retains all right, title and interest in Customer Data.
elements.evidence: The Company owns “all customer, order, transaction and user data generated through the Site in connection with Deerskin Products,” defined as Company Data, and receives all right, title and interest in it.

elements.element: The parties do not jointly own the deliverables, work product, Customer Data or other relevant IP.
elements.evidence: The clause expressly disclaims joint ownership of the Content, Site, Marks and Company Data; the Company's exclusive ownership of all other deliverables and work product also precludes joint ownership of those items.

elements.element: Vendor owns its generic tools.
elements.evidence: HDI retains only its pre-existing tools. The broad assignment of all deliverables and work product does not reserve to HDI generic tools developed under the Agreement.

elements.element: Vendor owns its know-how.
elements.evidence: The reservation covers only HDI's pre-existing know-how and does not reserve newly developed or generally applicable know-how.

elements.element: Customer is granted a licence covering the deliverables themselves.
elements.evidence: The Company owns the deliverables. The only express licence covers HDI materials incorporated in a deliverable, not the deliverable itself.

elements.element: The licence to the deliverables is perpetual.
elements.evidence: Although the embedded-HDI-materials licence is perpetual, no licence to the deliverables themselves is granted.

elements.element: The licence to the deliverables is irrevocable.
elements.evidence: Although the embedded-HDI-materials licence is irrevocable, no licence to the deliverables themselves is granted.

elements.element: The licence to the deliverables is worldwide.
elements.evidence: Although the embedded-HDI-materials licence is worldwide, no licence to the deliverables themselves is granted.

elements.element: The licence to the deliverables is royalty-free.
elements.evidence: Although the embedded-HDI-materials licence is royalty-free, no licence to the deliverables themselves is granted.

elements.element: The licence permits Customer to use the deliverables.
elements.evidence: The express right to use applies only to incorporated HDI materials, not to the deliverables as licensed subject matter.

elements.element: The licence permits Customer to modify the deliverables.
elements.evidence: The express right to modify applies only to incorporated HDI materials, not to the deliverables as licensed subject matter.

elements.element: The licence permits Customer to sublicense the deliverables.
elements.evidence: The express sublicensing right applies only to incorporated HDI materials, not to the deliverables as licensed subject matter.

elements.element: The licence permits Customer to exercise the licensed rights for its business.
elements.evidence: No licence to the deliverables themselves is granted, even though the incorporated-materials licence is not expressly restricted against business use.

result.reason: The operative language fully implements the preferred ownership structure, including assignment, retention of pre-existing HDI IP, an embedded-IP licence and exclusion of joint ownership. It does not implement the fallback's Vendor-ownership/licence structure because newly developed generic tools and know-how are not reserved and the express licence covers only incorporated HDI materials, not the deliverables themselves. The redline preserves the unrelated operational terms, but it is not minimal because it adds worldwide, modification and sublicensing rights and ownership provisions for Content and Marks beyond the preferred requirements. Drafting quality is reduced by overlap between the Company's purported ownership of the entire Site and HDI's retained embedded IP, the assignment's inclusion of assets HDI may never have owned, and the incomplete reservation for newly developed generic tools and know-how.
